generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The change from `ReadOnlyByteBufferBuf` to `ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf` requires ensuring that the new classes (`ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf`) are correctly handling all functionalities of their predecessors. Specifically, verify that these new classes maintain the read-only behavior and properly manage reference counts.

The removal of `allocator` and `buffer` from constructors indicates a change in how these objects are managed. Ensure that this change does not introduce memory leaks or improper resource management. Verify that the new approach correctly handles the lifecycle of the underlying buffer.

Changing `Unpooled.unmodifiableBuffer(unwrap().slice(index, length))` to `new ReadOnlyByteBuf(unwrap().slice(index, length))` should be verified for correctness. Ensure that `ReadOnlyByteBuf` maintains the read-only properties and behaves as expected when wrapping another buffer.

The addition of `asReadOnly()` method returning `this` is correct if the class already represents a read-only buffer. However, ensure that this method does not inadvertently allow modifications through other means.

review_comment: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
